title: Internship hunting
summary: Land an internship, SIWES placement or placement year: CV, LinkedIn, finding roles, applications, interviews and making the most of it.
description: Internships are where most students get their first real experience and, often, their first job offer. This roadmap covers the whole process from an empty CV to your last day on placement, including Nigeria's SIWES scheme and UK placement years.

stages.title: Get ready
stages.summary: Build the materials employers will look at.

stages.title: Find and apply
stages.summary: Find the right roles and send strong applications.

stages.title: Interview and start
stages.summary: Win the offer and make the placement count.

nodes.title: Write a student CV
nodes.description: One page that leads with education and relevant projects, uses bullet points that start with action verbs, and shows results with numbers where you can.

nodes.title: Set up LinkedIn
nodes.description: A clear photo, a headline that says what you study and what you're looking for, and your projects and coursework listed so recruiters find you.

resources.title: How to improve your LinkedIn profile (Prospects)

nodes.title: Build proof of skills
nodes.description: A small portfolio of projects, writing or case studies gives you something concrete to talk about when you have little work experience.

resources.title: How to get a job with no experience (Prospects)

nodes.title: Find internships and placements
nodes.description: Use your faculty's industrial training unit, careers service, company graduate pages and job boards. In Nigeria, SIWES placements are often found through department lists and alumni networks.

nodes.title: Applications and cover letters
nodes.description: Answer three questions in every cover letter: why this company, why this role, and why you. Keep it under a page and send it early, because many roles close once they fill.

resources.title: How to write a cover letter (Prospects)

nodes.title: Networking without the awkwardness
nodes.description: Short, specific messages to alumni and professionals asking for 15 minutes of advice open more doors than cold applications alone.

resources.title: Making the most of careers fairs (Prospects)

nodes.title: Interviews
nodes.description: Prepare five or six stories from your studies and activities, and practise telling them with the STAR method. Prepare questions to ask the interviewer too.

nodes.title: Make the placement count
nodes.description: Ask for clear goals in week one, keep a log of what you did and learned (you'll need it for SIWES reports and future CVs), and ask for feedback before you leave.
